title: Haussmann, by command
blurb: A Paris corner block (77 bd de Sébastopol, 1870) built to the engraved drawings, then a realism pass.
intro: The maison à loyer at N° 77 boulevard de Sébastopol, Paris (Paul Mesnard, published by César Daly in 1870), built to scale from the 1:100 elevation and 1:200 plans through the modelling command API: one plan n-gon extruded storey by storey, every opening an inset, cornices mitred round both cut corners, a 45° mansard by inset, railings on live curve arrays, dormers on live arrays. Then a short realism pass with the realism kit on the parts as built. Every dimension is measured back off the model.

hero.caption: From the rue Greneta corner, eye level

compareIntro: No geometry rebuilt (30-minute budget): the realism kit applied to the parts that exist. Stone: UVs at a 0.3 m tile and a tiling relief (the kit has no stone pattern yet, so its grain pattern stands in for tooled limestone). Roof and dormers: the metal-satin preset as zinc. Railings, balconettes and guards: metal-dark as wrought iron. Panes: screen-glass. Pavement: 1.2 m slab joints and a kerb line cut with groove (Manifold boolean). The facade itself could not take grooves for its rusticated courses: after the panes are separated it is an open shell (540 boundary edges), and groove cuts closed manifolds only; cut: false strips per pier would do it.

compare.caption: After: tooled-stone relief, zinc, wrought iron, coated glass, pavement joints

stills.caption: The 1870 elevation, registered at its scale bar (72.8 px/m)
Walls: one extrude per storey line - every bay is a quad
Openings: inset, recess, inset, separate the panes
The mansard: a 45° brisis (the 1859 limit) and a terrasson, by inset
The 2nd-floor balcony; the railing is one 30 cm module on a live curve array

metricsFirst: 388 commands headless in Node (no film), 0 failed, 21/21 checks
metrics: claude-opus-5-5 · 282 tool calls · 269k output / 140M input tokens
how:
build.mjs is the demo's session build script: measured data (pixel readings off Daly's plates, with the plate and row cited), then the build as commands, then the checks - each dimension measured off the model, not restated from constants. The realism pass is its own block at the end of the build (session.realism, on by default). record.mjs runs the unchanged build in examples/modelling-api on the GPU VM through demos/shared/session.mjs: its camera jumps become eased glides, each capture a held shot with its caption, each beat a title card; demos/shared/film.mjs renders and captures every frame. The shadow camera of the sun is sized to the block by the film (the light command has no parameter for it yet).

Re-run: node demos/haussmann/record.mjs then node demos/shared/report.mjs demos/haussmann. The plates and photographs come from refs/ (not committed; refs/SOURCES.md).
weak: Stone has no coursing: the rusticated ground floor and entresol (refends) need joint strips per pier, since the facade is an open shell after the panes are separated.
No mouldings: the cornice and string courses are stepped boxes (an inset with depth), not ogee/cyma profiles - the realism track's architecture parts (R3) are not built yet.
Window frames, shutters, shop fronts and the door are flat recessed panes; no mullions or glazing bars.
The kit has no stone or zinc presets and no stone relief pattern; the pass uses the plastic-grain relief and the satin-metal preset as stand-ins.
Lighting is one sun and the venice_sunset HDRI on a plain sky colour: no ambient occlusion, so recesses read shallow.
credits: César Daly, L'architecture privée au XIXe siècle (1870), Exemple M2 plates - public domain. Street photograph: rue Monge corner by Thierry Bézecourt (Thbz), CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.
